# What the data looks like {#sec-eda} ## Is there enough data? ::: {#tbl-volume .cell tbl-cap='Completed games by season, 2015–2025.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
games FBS vs FBS vs FCS team rows
season
2015 870 765 105 1530
2016 873 760 113 1520
2017 874 776 98 1552
2018 884 772 112 1544
2019 888 774 114 1548
2020 568 530 38 1060
2021 887 770 117 1540
2022 896 776 120 1552
2023 911 792 118 1584
2024 919 798 121 1596
2025 934 808 126 1616
total 9504 8321 1182 16642
``` ::: ::: The first model predicts **each team's points**, so every game gives two rows: 8\,321 FBS-vs-FBS games become 16\,642 training rows. That's plenty for linear models and enough for regularized gradient boosting, but it isn't big data. **Feature quality matters more than model complexity**, and that turned out to be the central lesson of the project. Games against FCS teams (1\,182, average margin ~31 points) are excluded from training. They're lopsided and not what we bet on. 2020 is small because of COVID cancellations. ## The target ::: {#cell-fig-targets .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Distribution of team points, game totals and home margins (FBS vs FBS, 2015–2025).](eda_files/figure-html/fig-targets-output-1.svg){#fig-targets} ::: ::: Team points average 27\.7 with a standard deviation of 13\.9. A model that always guesses the average misses by about 11 points. That's the floor every model has to clear. ::: {#cell-fig-key-numbers .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Share of games decided by exactly N points. Field goals (3) and touchdowns (7) dominate.](eda_files/figure-html/fig-key-numbers-output-1.svg){#fig-key-numbers} ::: ::: Margins cluster on **3 and 7**, so a normal distribution around a predicted margin isn't quite right when converting it into a probability of covering. ## Scoring is not stable over time ::: {#cell-fig-trend .cell execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Average game total by season (FBS vs FBS). The 2023 clock rule cut plays per game.](eda_files/figure-html/fig-trend-output-1.svg){#fig-trend} ::: ::: The average total fell by about 5 points between 2015 and 2025. The 2023 rule that keeps the clock running after first downs cut plays. Two consequences for features: **normalize by the season's league average** instead of using raw points, and **weigh recent seasons more** (recency decay in the ratings, @sec-features). ## Home field and quarters - **Home field:** home teams win by 4\.3 points at their own stadium and 1\.0 at neutral sites. - **Quarters are uneven:** Q1 12\.2, Q2 16\.3, Q3 12\.4, Q4 13\.9 points per game. Q2 is the highest-scoring quarter because of end-of-half drives. Overtime happens in 4\.4% of games.
